tools.name: sessions
tools.description: List sessions on disk, most recent first, with state, title, last_prompt and last_at. Use it to find a session id after an interrupted open.

status.description: OPENING | IDLE | RUNNING | ASKING | QUESTIONING | CLOSED

tools.name: open
tools.description: Open a session: reconnect when `session` is given; with `reuse`, take this server's idle session with the same cwd and subagent, else reconnect the latest closed one on disk; otherwise create one. A reuse that cannot reconnect creates a new session and says why in reuse_skipped. Reconnecting puts back the config the session last had (the subagent config, or later set_config changes). Returns once the session is set up (role prompt included), with the session id and the full config_options. It takes no task: send tasks with `prompt`.

role.description: Identity for the session. Avoid imperative verbs.

tools.name: prompt
tools.description: Send a task to an IDLE session. In ASKING or QUESTIONING it returns the pending approval or question instead. A session closed for idleness is reopened first. Blocks until the turn is done, needs an approval or asks a question; the server sets no time limit. If your client times out, the turn keeps running and the connection stays: call `status` for the state and `output` for the reply instead of sending the task again. Returns "approval_needed" with an approval to answer via approve / allow / reject, or "question_needed" with a question to answer via answer.

wait.description: Wait for the result (default true). false returns right after sending.

tools.name: approve
tools.description: Allow this one tool call (allow_once), or pick option_id explicitly. Blocks until the turn is done, needs an approval or asks a question; the server sets no time limit. If your client times out, the turn keeps running and the connection stays: call `status` for the state and `output` for the reply instead of sending the task again. Returns "approval_needed" with an approval to answer via approve / allow / reject, or "question_needed" with a question to answer via answer.

wait.description: Wait for the result (default true). false returns right after sending.

tools.name: allow
tools.description: Allow and stop asking for similar calls in this session only. Uses the agent's session-scoped option when it offers one; otherwise this server allows once and answers matching requests itself until the session closes. Never writes a persistent agent rule. Blocks until the turn is done, needs an approval or asks a question; the server sets no time limit. If your client times out, the turn keeps running and the connection stays: call `status` for the state and `output` for the reply instead of sending the task again. Returns "approval_needed" with an approval to answer via approve / allow / reject, or "question_needed" with a question to answer via answer.

wait.description: Wait for the result (default true). false returns right after sending.

tools.name: reject
tools.description: Reject this tool call (reject_once). Codex and Claude Code continue the turn; Grok and OpenCode end it as cancelled. Blocks until the turn is done, needs an approval or asks a question; the server sets no time limit. If your client times out, the turn keeps running and the connection stays: call `status` for the state and `output` for the reply instead of sending the task again. Returns "approval_needed" with an approval to answer via approve / allow / reject, or "question_needed" with a question to answer via answer.

wait.description: Wait for the result (default true). false returns right after sending.

tools.name: answer
tools.description: Answer a question the agent asked (question_needed). requested_schema is the agent's own form, passed on as sent: with action "accept" (the default), give content as an object whose keys and values follow it. "decline" refuses to answer, "cancel" dismisses the question. Blocks until the turn is done, needs an approval or asks a question; the server sets no time limit. If your client times out, the turn keeps running and the connection stays: call `status` for the state and `output` for the reply instead of sending the task again. Returns "approval_needed" with an approval to answer via approve / allow / reject, or "question_needed" with a question to answer via answer.

content.description: Field values for accept: string, number, boolean or an array of strings

wait.description: Wait for the result (default true). false returns right after sending.

tools.name: cancel
tools.description: Cancel the current turn. Returns "cancelling" until the agent confirms, or "done" when already idle.

tools.name: set_config
tools.description: Change a session config option (model, reasoning_effort, mode, ...). Returns the full config_options. Unknown ids or values fail with the available choices. A session closed for idleness is reopened first.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Session state, cancelling flag, current config values, pending approvals and questions, and whether a blocking call is waiting. Cheap to call repeatedly; the config choices are in open, set_config and snapshot. A session closed for idleness reports CLOSED with its last values.

tools.name: progress
tools.description: The agent's latest execution feedback: its plan, context usage, session title and slash commands. Not needed to run a task; call it only when you want to know. Cheap, never blocks.

tools.name: output
tools.description: Final reply of the most recent turn.

tools.name: close
tools.description: Close a session, or all sessions of this server when session is omitted. Session history is kept.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Delete a session and its native agent session (deleted / archived / unsupported).

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Full conversation of open sessions, the same as the webui shows: prompts, replies, thinking, tool calls with their input, output and diffs, plans, approvals, questions and agent-specific messages, plus each session's state and pending notifications. It can be large: pass session, and use last, types or exclude_types to keep it small. Pass back server_id and seq as since to get only what changed. ack is for UI clients that relay notifications. UI clients that poll: pass simplify to leave out tool call details (input, output, content) and session commands, and get one item in full with item.

since.description: seq from the previous call: only items changed after it

server_id.description: server_id from the previous call; a different one resets

last.description: Only the last n items, after the kind filters

simplify.description: Tool items keep only their title, status and other header fields; commands are left out

tools.name: item
tools.description: One conversation item in full, by the id snapshot gave it: a tool call with its input, output and diffs, or any other item. For UI clients that poll snapshot with simplify and show details on demand.
